newsitem.title: DUBAI: Saudi cenbank warns on unlicensed investment firms.
newsitem.headline: Saudi cenbank warns on unlicensed investment firms.

text.p: Saudi Arabian Monetary Agency Governor Hamad Saud al-Sayyari warned, in remarks published on Wednesday, against dealing with unlicensed investment firms.

"Our public should safeguard its interests by not dealing with unlicensed and unsupervised entities offering investment services and products," Sayyari said in an interview with the Arab News. Only Saudi banks were licensed to offer these services, he said.
"We are aware of a number of unlicensed entities operating within the kingdom and in conjunction with other government agencies, we are actively working to curtail their activities."
Sayyari said the Saudi banking system, which is made up of 12 banks and 1,207 branches, was "facing increasing challenges both from domestic and international quarters".

Domestic challenges "stem from the need to advance the banking habits of Saudi customers in general, to protect small customers, to enhance competition for greater efficiency, to introduce advanced technology and to provide a broad range of products and services", he said.
The governor said another challenge was the enhancement of a sound regulatory framework.

Internationally "our challenges include adapting to increased competition from international banks and financial institutions while protecting smaller investors from unscrupulous individuals and institutions", he said.

Sayyari said 58 percent of the banking sector's workforce were Saudis. The kingdom, like many of its Gulf Arab neighbours, is trying to reduce dependence on expatriate workers and find jobs for its own nationals.
